title: Hybrid INT8/FP8 validation runner with stochastic perturbation tests
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build an automated validation runner that evaluates hybrid quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8 variants) using a mix of deterministic golden prompt checks and stochastic perturbation tests. The runner should: 1) load a candidate quant profile and associated model artifacts, 2) run deterministic golden-prompt comparisons for baseline pass/fail, 3) execute randomized perturbation trials (token-level noise, prompt paraphrases, temperature sweeps) to surface brittle failure modes, 4) compute a composite score (KL + token-level PERP + semantic similarity) and apply dynamic pass/fail gates, 5) emit detailed telemetry and a human-readable summary for release engineers. The goal is to catch regressions introduced by calibration or new kernel selection before dedicated or hosted rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Runner accepts a profile bundle (model, quant config, calibration artifacts) and completes end-to-end pipeline in < 45 minutes on CI staging hardware
Deterministic golden checks produce bit-level diffs and aggregated metric table; pass threshold default KL < 0.015 and token PERP delta < 1.2x
Stochastic perturbation suite runs 200 randomized trials and reports a failure if > 5% of trials exceed per-trial thresholds
Composite pass/fail decision exported to a machine-readable artifact (JSON) and uploaded to S3 and the validation dashboard
Telemetry includes per-layer activation drift, per-head sensitivity markers, and a replayable seed list so flakiness can be reproduced locally
implementation_notes: Pipeline stages: (A) preflight: sanity-check shapes, kv cache warmup; (B) deterministic replay: run golden corpus with beam=1+sampling disabled; (C) perturbation ambient: add token-level logits noise, paraphrase prompts via LLM paraphraser, vary decoding temperature 0.0-1.2; (D) metrics: compute KL across token distributions, token PERP, BERTScore/embedding-sim; (E) gating: dynamic thresholds influenced by latency and model class. Use existing calibration artifacts from s3://redwood-quant/artifacts/ and reuse the quant-eval harness library. Where latency increases > 10% vs baseline, flag for manual review.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Stochastic tests can be flaky and produce noisy failures - Mitigation: enforce reproducibility via seeded RNGs and require >1 failing seed to mark profile as failed
Risk: Long runtime on large models - Mitigation: sample smaller representative golden set, increase parallelism, and set runtime budget cap in config
Risk: Metrics sensitive to decoding changes rather than quantization - Mitigation: run paired delta tests (same decode settings) and include a baseline float run for comparison
Risk: Storage cost for detailed token-level telemetry - Mitigation: keep token-level diffs for N days (configurable), compress and store aggregated summaries by default
